mainTopic: When a lost חטאת (or its money) is left to die: what counts as 'lost,' רב פפא's questions, and the new משנה's dispute between רבי and חכמים.
overview: The amud begins with רבא's rule that a חטאת lost only at night does not count as 'lost.' The גמרא first fits this to רבי, and then offers a second reading that fits it to רבנן, about an animal still missing at the time of atonement. אביי adds a tradition: only a lost חטאת is left to die, not a stolen or robbed one. The גמרא then defines 'lost': an animal mixed into the flock counts, but if the owner or the shepherd can identify it, it is not lost. Two of these questions end with תיקו. רב פפא asks about an animal found while the replacement's blood is already in the cup. The גמרא explains his question in two ways, and it ends with תיקו. A new משנה lists cases of a lost חטאת or lost money that was replaced. It brings the dispute between רבי and חכמים over whether the extra animal dies even before the owner got כפרה. The גמרא then notices that the רישא of the משנה fits רבנן while the סיפא fits רבי. It begins to answer using רב הונא in the name of רב, and that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא: An animal lost at night is not called lost
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבא's statement that a חטאת lost only at night does not have the status of a 'lost' animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself: רבא said that an animal lost at night is not called 'lost.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a statement of רבא that was mentioned earlier so it can examine it. רבא says that a חטאת that went missing at night does not count as 'lost.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule about a lost חטאת: in certain cases it is left to die. רבא says that going missing at night does not trigger that 'lost' status. This is because at night no offering can be brought anyway, so nothing was really missed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא now examines a statement it quoted earlier
A lost animal, here a lost חטאת
It is not called / does not have the status of

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rava said:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to a line of רבא that it quoted a bit earlier, to look at it closely now.

phrases.english: An animal lost at night is not called 'lost.'
phrases.notes: He is talking about a חטאת that went missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by restating רבא's ruling for analysis.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת that went missing only at night is not considered 'lost.'

steps.title: Whose opinion does רבא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which side of the dispute in the משנה רבא's statement fits.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom did רבא say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: which opinion is רבא following? This sets up the next move, where the גמרא tries out each option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי and רבנן argue about when a lost חטאת is left to die. רבא's statement has to fit one of them. The גמרא wants to know which one.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whose opinion?

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which opinion the statement in step 1 follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבא's statement follows רבי or רבנן.

steps.title: It can't be the רבנן, since for them even day-loss leads to grazing
steps.stepSummary: If רבא follows רבנן, why mention night? According to רבנן, even an animal lost by day goes to graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say רבא follows רבנן, why does he talk only about night? Even an animal lost by day would be the same, because רבנן say that an animal lost at the time another was set aside goes to graze.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the idea that רבא follows רבנן and finds a problem. For רבנן, even an animal lost by day is treated leniently, so 'at night' would be a pointless detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן say that being lost when the replacement was designated is not enough to make the animal die. It only goes to graze. So for them, being lost at night would obviously not make it die either, and רבא's point would add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? (implies the detail is unnecessary)
Designating (setting aside) a replacement animal
Grazes: left to graze until it gets a blemish, then sold

phrases.english: If you say according to the Rabbis —
why specifically one lost at night?
Even one lost by day is also the same,
for the Rabbis say:
one lost at the time of designation grazes.
phrases.notes: This is רבנן's view in the משנה: it does not die unless it was still missing when the owner got atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן מַאי אִירְיָא אֲבוּדָה דְּלַיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first possible answer to step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבא's statement follows רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבנן, even a day-loss at the time of designation only leads to grazing, so the 'night' detail would be pointless.

steps.title: רבא follows רבי: even he agrees about night-loss
steps.stepSummary: רבא follows רבי. רבי is strict only about an animal lost by day; for one lost at night, even רבי agrees it goes to graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא follows רבי. רבי only said his strict ruling about an animal lost during the day. But about an animal lost at night, even רבי agrees that it goes to graze.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא is explaining the opinion of רבי. He shows that רבי's strict rule has a limit: it does not cover an animal lost at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that being lost at the moment of designation makes the animal die. רבא adds that this applies only to a daytime loss. A night loss does not count as 'lost,' so now the 'night' detail has real meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said his ruling in this case (limits the opinion)
Agrees
It goes to grazing

phrases.english: Rather, it is according to Rabbi,
Rabbi only said his ruling
about an animal lost by day,
but an animal lost at night —
even Rabbi agrees
that it goes to graze.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to step 2 after step 3 ruled out רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא follows רבי and limits רבי's strict ruling to an animal lost by day.

steps.title: רבא follows the רבנן, about an animal missing at the time of atonement
steps.stepSummary: Another option: רבא follows רבנן. He is talking about an animal still missing when the owner got atonement. רבנן say such an animal dies only if it first went missing by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: really רבא follows רבנן. We are dealing with an animal that was still missing at the time of atonement. רבנן only said that such an animal dies when it first got lost during the day. But if it first got lost at night, it does not die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second answer that keeps רבא with רבנן after all. It says רבא is talking about a different moment: the time of atonement, not the time of designation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן, the case where the animal dies is when it is still missing at atonement. רבא limits this: it applies only if the loss first began by day. If the animal first disappeared at night, it never got 'lost' status, so even being missing at atonement does not make it die.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces an alternative answer
Really / actually (returns to an option that was rejected)
What case are we dealing with here?
The time the owner gets atonement with the other animal
It is left to die
The start of its loss: when it first went missing

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two moments. רבי's dispute with רבנן is about being lost at the time of designation (הפרשה). This answer is about being lost at the time of atonement (כפרה).
steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to read רבא: (1) according to רבי, a night-loss at designation does not make the animal die; (2) according to רבנן, even if the animal is missing at atonement, it does not die if it first went missing at night.

phrases.english: If you want, say:
really it is according to the Rabbis,
and what are we dealing with here?
With one that was lost at the time of atonement.
The Rabbis only said
'one lost at the time of atonement dies'
where its loss first began by day,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּעִיקַּר אֲבֵידָתָהּ בַּלַּיְלָה — לָא.
phrases.english: but where its loss first began at night — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer instead of step 4, rescuing the רבנן option rejected in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifting the case: lost at the time of atonement, not designation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא could not follow רבנן, since for them a day-loss at designation already leads to grazing.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא follows רבנן about an animal missing at atonement: it dies only if the loss began by day.

steps.title: אביי: Only lost, not stolen or robbed
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a tradition: the rule that a lost חטאת dies applies only to a lost animal, not to a stolen or robbed one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition: 'lost,' but not stolen; 'lost,' but not robbed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a new rule. The harsh 'left to die' law applies only to a חטאת that was lost, not to one that was stolen or taken by force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stealing (secretly) and robbing (openly, by force) are not the same as losing. So a stolen or robbed חטאת that comes back after the owner's atonement is not left to die. It goes to graze instead.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold / we have a tradition
Stolen (taken secretly)
Robbed (taken openly, by force)

steps.whyThisMatters: It narrows the 'lost חטאת dies' rule to a real loss only, which matters for practical cases of theft.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We have a tradition:
lost, but not stolen;
lost, but not robbed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a separate rule about what counts as a 'lost' חטאת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a lost חטאת is left to die; a stolen or robbed one is not.

steps.title: What counts as a lost animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the definition of a 'lost' animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly is a 'lost' animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what situation counts as 'lost' for the rule about a lost חטאת. This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps discussed when a lost חטאת is left to die. Now the גמרא needs to define 'lost', because the rule depends on it. Does it mean gone far away, or simply not identifiable?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
A lost item or animal

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of a 'lost' animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי limited the rule to a lost animal, the גמרא defines what 'lost' means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of 'lost' for a חטאת.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: even one mixed into the flock
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא says a חטאת that cannot be told apart from other animals counts as lost, even if it is mixed with just one other animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: Even one animal mixed into his flock, and even one mixed with one other, counts as lost.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא answers: an animal counts as lost even if it is right there in the owner's flock, as long as he cannot tell which one it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Lost' does not need to mean physically gone. If the owner cannot identify which animal is the חטאת, it counts as lost. This is true even if it is mixed with only one other animal.

keyTerms.meaning: His flock
One mixed with one other

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
Even one in his flock,
phrases.notes: He means the חטאת got mixed into his flock, and now he can't tell which animal it is.

phrases.english: and even one with one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אֲפִילּוּ אַחַת בְּעֶדְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Being mixed in so that it cannot be identified counts as lost, even if it is mixed with just one other animal.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even behind the door
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says an animal behind the door counts as lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Behind the door.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives his own definition: an animal that is 'behind the door' counts as lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's case is an animal that is close by but out of view. His words are short, so the next step asks what exactly he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Behind the door

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Behind the door.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An animal behind the door counts as lost.

steps.title: What did רבי יוחנן mean by 'behind the door'? Unresolved
steps.stepSummary: Is 'behind the door' the only case of lost, or the smallest case, so that outside is surely lost too? The question stays unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: What does he mean? Is it only behind the door, where nobody sees it, that it is lost, but outside, where people see it, it is not lost? Or perhaps even behind the door, where he would see it if he turned around, it is lost, and all the more so outside, where he does not see it? It stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן's 'behind the door' is a strict limit or just the easiest example. It cannot decide, so it ends with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: behind the door counts because no one sees it there, so an animal outside among people is not lost. Option two: behind the door is lost even though one turn of the head would reveal it, so outside is surely lost. The answer is not found.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים
Outside
All the more so
Let it stand; the question is left unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: The two readings flip the result for an animal outside. In the first reading it is NOT lost. In the second it is lost all the more so.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
How is he saying it?
Is it behind the door
where there is no one who sees it,
but outside, where there are people who see it,
it is not considered lost?
Or perhaps even behind the door,
where if he turned his face he would see it,
it is considered lost,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן אַבָּרַאי דְּלָא קָחָזֵי לַהּ?
phrases.english: and all the more so outside, where he does not see it?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what רבי יוחנן's short statement in step 9 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'behind the door' is the limit of lost or the smallest example of it.

steps.title: רב פפא: if the shepherd knows it, it is not lost
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reports a tradition: if the owner cannot identify the animal but the shepherd can, it is not lost. If the shepherd cannot but the owner can, it is surely not lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We have a tradition: lost from the owner but not from his shepherd, it is not lost. All the more so, lost from the shepherd but not from the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a set rule: as long as either the owner or the shepherd knows which animal it is, it does not count as lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowledge by the shepherd is enough to keep the animal from being lost. If the owner himself knows, it is all the more so not lost.

keyTerms.meaning: We have learned this as a tradition
Its shepherd
From him (the owner)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: We have learned as a tradition:
lost from him but not from its shepherd,
it is not considered lost,
and all the more so, lost from its shepherd
but not lost from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another detail to the definition of 'lost'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If either the owner or the shepherd can identify the animal, it is not lost.

steps.title: What if only someone far away recognizes it? Unresolved
steps.stepSummary: If neither owner nor shepherd knows it, but someone at the end of the world recognizes it, is it lost? תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lost from him and from its shepherd, but one person at the end of the world recognizes it: what is the law? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes רב פפא's rule one step further and asks about a faraway person who can identify the animal. It cannot decide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shepherd's knowledge counts. Does any person's knowledge count, even someone far away? The question is left open with תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: The end of the world; very far away
Recognizes

phrases.english: Lost from him and from its shepherd,
and one person at the end of the world recognizes it,
what is the law? Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבוּדָה מִמֶּנּוּ וּמֵרוֹעָהּ וְאֶחָד בְּסוֹף הָעוֹלָם מַכִּיר בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the tradition of step 11 to a harder case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a faraway person's recognition keeps the animal from being lost.
steps.whatToRemember: An animal that cannot be identified counts as lost. If the owner or the shepherd knows it, it is not lost. Two cases stay open: what רבי יוחנן meant, and the faraway recognizer.

steps.title: רב פפא asks about an animal found when the blood is in the cup
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks what the law is when the lost חטאת is found while the replacement's blood is already in the cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: What is the law of an animal 'lost at the cup'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא opens a new question. The lost animal was replaced, the replacement was slaughtered, and the original turned up while the blood was in the cup, waiting to be sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether that moment counts as the animal being 'lost' at the key time of atonement. The status of the original animal depends on this.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question
The cup that holds the blood before it is sprinkled
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
An animal lost at the cup, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means the original was still missing while the replacement's blood was in the cup, and was found then.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא אֲבוּדָה בַּכּוֹס מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question about the timing of 'lost'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The status of a חטאת found while the replacement's blood is in the cup.

steps.title: Whose opinion is רב פפא's question based on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which side of the dispute רב פפא's question follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which opinion רב פפא's question is based on. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A question only makes sense if the answer is not already obvious according to that opinion. So the גמרא checks each side of the dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whose opinion?

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of רב פפא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion רב פפא's question follows.

steps.title: It cannot follow רבי
steps.stepSummary: If the question followed רבי, there would be nothing to ask. רבי holds that even an animal lost only at the time the replacement was designated is left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it follows רבי, didn't he say that an animal lost at the time of designation dies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, רבי. It shows that the question does not work for רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, being lost at the earlier moment of designating the replacement is already enough for the animal to die. So it surely dies if it was still lost later, at the cup, and there is no question.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say
The time of designating the replacement animal

phrases.english: If you say it follows Rabbi,
didn't he say that one lost at the time of designation dies!
phrases.notes: Designation comes before the blood is in the cup, so for רבי the later moment is surely covered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי הָאָמַר אֲבוּדָה בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה מֵתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules out the first possible answer to step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רב פפא's question follows רבי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי already says the animal dies if it was lost at the earlier time of designation, so being lost at the later time of the cup is obviously enough. There is nothing to ask.

steps.title: The question follows the Rabbis: is blood in the cup as good as sprinkled?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves רב פפא's question to the view of the רבנן. It opens the first side: maybe 'it grazes' only applies before the blood is collected, because blood ready to be sprinkled counts as already sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he asks according to the רבנן. Do we say that when the רבנן said an animal lost at the time of designation goes out to graze, that is only before the blood of the other animal was collected in a cup? But here, they hold that whatever stands ready to be sprinkled is considered as if it was already sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 15 by saying רב פפא asked his question according to the רבנן, not רבי. It then lays out the first side of his question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say a חטאת lost when the replacement was designated is left to graze, not to die. The new question is about timing. Once the replacement's blood is in the cup and ready to be sprinkled, it might already count as sprinkled, as if atonement had already happened. If so, the found animal would be treated more harshly.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything standing ready to be sprinkled is treated as if it was already sprinkled
At the time the replacement animal was designated
It grazes: left in the pasture until it gets a blemish, then redeemed
Before the blood is collected in the cup (the service vessel)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Grazes' (רוֹעָה) is the lenient outcome and 'dies' is the strict one. The question is whether having the blood in the cup pushes the case from grazing toward dying.

phrases.english: Rather, when he raises the question,
it is according to the Rabbis:
Do we say:
when the Rabbis said
that one lost at the time of designation grazes,
that is before one collects the blood in the cup,
but here they hold:
whatever stands ready to be sprinkled
is considered as if sprinkled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of step 15 by moving the question to the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the question to the other side of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was assumed to follow רבי, where it has an obvious answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question follows the רבנן: does 'grazing' still apply once the replacement's blood is in the cup?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether blood standing ready to be sprinkled already counts as sprinkled for this case.

steps.title: Or maybe it is still like lost at designation and grazes
steps.stepSummary: The second side of the question: as long as the blood has not actually been sprinkled, the case is still like an animal lost at the time of designation, so it grazes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps, as long as the blood has not been sprinkled, it is like an animal lost at the time of designation, and it grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב פפא's question by giving the other possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this side, only actual sprinkling counts, and blood sitting in the cup changes nothing. The found animal is then treated like any animal lost at designation according to the רבנן: it grazes and does not die.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps: introduces the second side of a question
Was sprinkled (on the altar)

phrases.english: Or perhaps,
as long as the blood has not been sprinkled,
it is like one lost at the time of designation,
and it grazes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא, כְּמָה דְּלָא אִזְדְּרִיק דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question begun in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether only actual sprinkling, not collection, ends the 'lost at designation' status.

steps.title: A second version: the question follows רבי, with two cups of blood
steps.stepSummary: Some say the question really does follow רבי, but the case is different: the blood of one animal was collected in two cups, and one cup was lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: really, it follows רבי. When he asks, it is about a case where the blood was collected in two cups and one of them was lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to step 15. It keeps the question within רבי's view but changes the case to one animal's blood in two cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15's problem was that for רבי, two animals with one lost at designation is already clear: the lost one dies. Here there is only one animal, and the 'lost' item is a cup of its blood. רבי's rule about lost animals might or might not apply to a lost cup of blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in fact: keeps the original assumption
In two cups: the blood of one offering collected in two vessels

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is a second way of explaining רב פפא's same question, as an alternative to steps 16 and 17.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
Actually, it follows רבי,
and when he raises the question,
it is where he collected its blood in two cups,
and one of them was lost.
phrases.notes: The cup went missing when the כהן sprinkled the blood from the other cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to step 15, instead of the answer in steps 16 and 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was assumed to be about two separate animals, which is obvious for רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about one animal's blood split into two cups, which is open even for רבי.

steps.title: The question only works for the view that the second cup is leftover blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the second version. There is no question for the view that one cup makes the other rejected. The question exists only for the view that one cup makes the other שיריים (leftover blood).
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says one cup makes the other rejected, you should not ask. Ask according to the one who says one cup makes the other a remainder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies which opinion the two-cups version of the question depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second cup is דחוי (rejected), its blood is unusable anyway, so there is nothing to ask. If it is only שיריים (leftover blood, poured at the altar's base), then it still has some status. The question is whether being lost changes it from leftover to rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: One cup makes the other cup rejected (unusable)
One cup makes the other cup leftover blood, poured at the altar's base
You need not ask: the answer is obvious under this view

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רב פפא's question. (1) It follows the רבנן: does blood in the cup count as sprinkled? (2) It follows רבי with two cups of one animal's blood, and this works only for the view that the other cup becomes שיריים.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says
one cup makes its fellow rejected,
you should not ask;
when should you ask?
According to the one who says
one cup makes its fellow a remainder.
phrases.notes: A 'remainder' is leftover blood that gets poured out at the base of the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר כּוֹס עוֹשֶׂה חֲבֵירוֹ דָּחוּי לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the two-cups version from step 18 to a specific opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two-cups question applies only according to the view that one cup makes the other שיריים, not דחוי.

steps.title: Does the two-cup rule apply when one cup is missing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the question. Maybe the second cup counts only as שיריים when both cups are there, because the כהן can sprinkle from either one. But when one cup is lost, maybe things are different. Or maybe it makes no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this rule apply only where both cups are present, since he can sprinkle from whichever one he wants? But here, that cup is missing. Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out both sides of the question within the view that one cup makes the other שיריים: does that view still hold when one of the cups is lost?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'שיריים' view seems to rest on a choice: with both cups present, the כהן may sprinkle from either, so neither cup is pushed aside. Once one cup is lost there is no longer a choice, so maybe the lost cup counts as נדחה (rejected). The other side says the rule does not depend on having a choice.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover blood, which is not the main blood for sprinkling but is not disqualified either
Rejected or pushed aside, so it can no longer be used
He sprinkles (the blood on the מזבח)
It makes no difference

steps.confusionAlert: This question is asked only within the view that one cup makes the other שיריים. For the view that one cup makes the other נדחה, there was never a question (step 19).

phrases.english: Does this statement apply
phrases.notes: 'This statement' is the view that the second cup counts as שיריים (step 19).

phrases.english: only where both cups are present,
since he may sprinkle from whichever one he wants;
but here, that cup is not present,
phrases.notes: Since one cup is lost, the כהן has no choice left, so maybe the lost cup counts as rejected.

phrases.english: or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the actual content of the question that step 19 narrowed to the 'שיריים' view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule that the second cup is only שיריים depend on both cups being present, so that a lost cup becomes נדחה?

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot settle the question, so it ends with תיקו: the question stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the whole discussion of רב פפא's question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source is found that decides between the two sides. תיקו means the question stays open, with no ruling either way from this sugya.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רב פפא's question. In one it follows the רבנן: does blood in the cup count as already sprinkled? In the other it follows רבי: one animal's blood in two cups, with one cup lost, asked only within the 'שיריים' view. No answer is given in either version, and the discussion ends with תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question raised in step 20 without a resolution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a lost cup of blood counts as rejected under the 'שיריים' view stays undecided.

steps.title: A lost חטאת found after a replacement was set aside
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. Someone set aside a חטאת, it got lost, and he set aside another animal in its place. If the first animal is found afterward, it is left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone sets aside a sin offering, it gets lost, and he sets aside another in its place, and afterward the first one is found, it must be left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new משנה. Its first case is a lost חטאת that turns up after a replacement animal was set aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The found original חטאת is not offered. Instead it is left to die (תמות). The גמרא (step 32) reads this case as one where the replacement was already offered. If the replacement had only been set aside, the original would graze.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
One who sets aside (designates) something for a קרבן
Sin offering
It shall die; it is locked away until it dies and is not offered or used

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who designates a sin offering, and it was lost,
and he designated another in its place,
and afterward the first one was found,
it shall be left to die.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת וְאָבְדָה וְהִפְרִישׁ אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended with תיקו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lost חטאת found after a replacement was set aside and offered is left to die.

steps.title: Lost money for a חטאת found after an animal replaced it
steps.stepSummary: Someone set aside money to buy a חטאת, and the money was lost. He then set aside an animal as a חטאת instead. If the money is found later, he must throw it into the Dead Sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sets aside money for his sin offering, it gets lost, and he sets aside a sin offering animal in its place, and afterward the money is found, he must take it to the Dead Sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. This time money, not an animal, was lost and then replaced by an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The found money has the same status as a חטאת that is left to die, so no one may use it. Throwing it into the Dead Sea makes sure nobody can ever benefit from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Money (coins)
The Dead Sea; throwing something there destroys it so no one can use it
He shall take them

phrases.english: One who designates money for his sin offering,
and it was lost, and he designated a sin offering in its place,
and afterward the money was found,
he must take it to the Dead Sea.
phrases.notes: The money is treated like a חטאת that is left to die, so it is destroyed and no one gets any benefit from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת לְחַטָּאתוֹ וְאָבְדוּ וְהִפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת תַּחְתֵּיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the idea of the first case to money that was replaced by an animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lost money for a חטאת, found after an animal was set aside in its place, must be destroyed in the Dead Sea.

steps.title: Lost money found before the replacement money was used
steps.stepSummary: Someone set aside money for a חטאת, lost it, and set aside other money in its place. Before he managed to buy an animal, the first money was found. He buys a חטאת using both sets of money, and the rest goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sets aside money for a sin offering, it gets lost, and he sets aside other money in its place, but before he manages to buy a sin offering with it the first money is found, he brings a sin offering from both, and the rest goes to voluntary offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third case. Here the replacement was money, and no animal had been bought yet when the first money was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no animal was bought yet, neither set of money is pushed aside, so the משנה does not send either one to the Dead Sea. He buys one חטאת from the combined money, and the leftover money is used for נדבה offerings instead of being destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not manage (in time)
The rest, the leftover
Voluntary (gift) offerings

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three cases. A found animal is left to die. Found money, after an animal was set aside in its place, goes to the Dead Sea. Found money, before the replacement money was used, is combined with it for one חטאת, and the rest goes to נדבה.

phrases.english: One who designates money for a sin offering,
and it was lost, and he designated other money in its place,
and he did not manage to buy a sin offering with it
before the first money was found,
he should bring a sin offering from both this money and that money,
and the rest shall go to voluntary offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת לְחַטָּאת וְאָבְדוּ וְהִפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת אֲחֵרוֹת תַּחְתֵּיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes the case from step 23: the replacement was money that had not yet been used to buy an animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the first money is found before the replacement money is used, one חטאת is bought from both, and the leftover goes to נדבה.

steps.title: Lost money is found, but the replacement animal has a blemish
steps.stepSummary: Money for a חטאת was lost and an animal was set aside instead. The money was found before the animal was brought, and the animal has a מום. The animal is sold, both sums together buy a חטאת, and the extra goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone set aside money for his חטאת and it was lost, and he set aside an animal as a חטאת instead, and before he could bring it the money was found, and that animal has a blemish: the animal is sold, he brings a חטאת using both sums of money, and whatever is left goes to נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case that looks like the one in step 23. The difference is that here the replacement animal has a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23 the replacement animal was fine, so the found money went to ים המלח. Here the animal cannot be brought because of its blemish, so it is sold for money. Now he has two sums of money, and they are joined to buy one חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Money (here, money set aside to buy a חטאת)
An animal with a blemish that cannot be brought on the מזבח
It shall be sold
From these and from those: using both sums together
Go to the fund for voluntary (gift) offerings

phrases.english: One who sets aside money for his sin offering, and it was lost,
and he set aside a sin offering in its place,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִסְפִּיק לְהַקְרִיבָהּ עַד שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ הַמָּעוֹת,
phrases.english: he did not manage to offer it before the money was found,
and the sin offering has a blemish: it is sold,
and he brings a sin offering from this and from that,
phrases.notes: This means the found money plus the money from selling the blemished animal.

phrases.english: and the rest goes to gift offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of lost-חטאת cases in the משנה and changes step 23's case by giving the replacement animal a blemish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the replacement animal is a בעל מום, it is sold. The found money and the sale money together buy one חטאת, and the extra goes to נדבה.

steps.title: Lost animal is found with a blemish after money was set aside instead
steps.stepSummary: A חטאת animal was lost and money was set aside instead. The animal was found before a new one was bought, and it has a מום. The animal is sold, both sums buy a חטאת, and the extra goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone set aside a חטאת and it was lost, and he set aside money instead, and before he could buy a חטאת with it his first animal was found, and it has a blemish: it is sold, he brings a חטאת using both sums, and whatever is left goes to נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the last case. Now the animal is what got lost, and money was set aside to replace it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal that comes back has a blemish, so it cannot be brought. It is sold, and again there are two sums of money. The ruling is the same: join them for one חטאת and send the rest to נדבה.

keyTerms.meaning: To buy (literally, to take)
In its place
A female animal with a blemish (the feminine form of בעל מום)

phrases.english: One who sets aside a sin offering, and it was lost,
and he set aside money in its place,
and he did not manage to buy a sin offering with it
before his sin offering was found,
and it has a blemish: it is sold,
and he brings a sin offering from this and from that,
and the rest goes to gift offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת וְאָבְדָה, וְהִפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת תַּחְתֶּיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 25: here the animal is lost and replaced by money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The found blemished animal is sold. Its money and the replacement money together buy one חטאת, and the extra goes to נדבה.

steps.title: Both the lost animal and its replacement have blemishes
steps.stepSummary: A חטאת was lost and another animal was set aside. The first one was found, and both have a מום. Both are sold, the money from both buys a חטאת, and the extra goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone set aside his חטאת and it was lost, and he set aside another one instead, and before he could bring it the first was found, and both have blemishes: both are sold, he brings a חטאת with money from both, and whatever is left goes to נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now takes the case of step 22, where an animal replaced an animal, but here both animals have a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22 the first animal was left to die because the second had already been offered. Here neither one can be brought, so both are sold. The two sums together buy one new חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Another (animal)
Both of them
They are sold

phrases.english: One who sets aside his sin offering, and it was lost,
and he set aside another in its place,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִסְפִּיק לְהַקְרִיבָהּ עַד שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה,
phrases.english: he did not manage to offer it before the first one was found,
and both of them have a blemish: they are sold,
and he brings a sin offering from this and from that,
phrases.notes: He buys a third animal using the money from selling both blemished ones.

phrases.english: and the rest goes to gift offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the animal-for-animal case of step 22, now with both animals blemished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both animals are blemished, both are sold and the money is joined to buy one חטאת. The extra goes to נדבה.

steps.title: Both animals are unblemished: רבי says one is brought and the other dies
steps.stepSummary: The same case, but both animals are fit to be brought. רבי rules that one is brought as a חטאת and the other is left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone set aside a חטאת and it was lost, and he set aside another one instead, and before he could bring it the first was found, and both are without blemish: one is brought as a חטאת and the other is left to die. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the last case: both animals are perfect. It also tells us that the rule of leaving one to die is the view of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since only one חטאת is needed and both animals can be brought, one is used and the extra one is left to die, even though it was found before the owner got כפרה. The משנה tells us this ruling is רבי's opinion, and the next step brings חכמים, who disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Without blemish, fit for the מזבח
Will be offered
Will be left to die

phrases.english: One who sets aside a sin offering, and it was lost,
and he set aside another in its place,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִסְפִּיק לְהַקְרִיבָהּ עַד שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה,
phrases.english: he did not manage to offer it before the first one was found,
if both of them were unblemished:
one of them is offered as a sin offering,
and the second is left to die; these are the words of Rabbi.
phrases.notes: "רבי" on his own means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the set of cases with both animals fit, and names רבי as the source of this ruling that the extra animal dies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: when both animals are fit, one is brought as a חטאת and the other is left to die.

steps.title: חכמים: a חטאת dies only if found after the owner got his כפרה
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי. A חטאת is left to die, and money is thrown into ים המלח, only if it was found after the owner already brought his offering and got כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים say: a חטאת is not left to die unless it was found after the owners already got their כפרה. And money is not thrown into ים המלח unless it was found after the owners already got their כפרה.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים argue with רבי. They limit the harsh rules of leaving a חטאת to die and throwing money into ים המלח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the extra item is lost even if it was found before the owner brought his offering. For חכמים, that only happens if it turned up after the כפרה was already done. So in the cases above, where things were found before the offering was brought, חכמים would not have the extra animal die or the money go to ים המלח.

keyTerms.meaning: Not... unless / only when
Is left to die
The owners already got their כפרה (their offering was already brought)
The Dead Sea, where forbidden money is thrown so no one can use it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: an extra חטאת or extra חטאת money is lost even if found before the כפרה. חכמים: only if it was found after the owner already got his כפרה.
steps.confusionAlert: חכמים are not saying the found animal is brought too. They are only limiting when it is left to die. Their rule depends on whether it was found before or after the כפרה.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
A sin offering is not left to die
unless it was found after the owners achieved atonement,
and the money does not go to the Dead Sea
unless it was found after the owners achieved atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין חַטָּאת מֵתָה אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת מֵאַחַר שֶׁכִּיפְּרוּ הַבְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי in step 28, and also limits the rulings of steps 22 and 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: a חטאת is left to die, and money goes to ים המלח, only when it was found after the owner already got his כפרה.

steps.title: A blemished חטאת is sold and replaced
steps.stepSummary: If someone sets aside a חטאת and it has a מום, he sells it and uses the money to buy another חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person sets aside an animal as a חטאת and it has a blemish, he sells it and brings a different animal with the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its last case. A חטאת that has a מום cannot be brought, so it is sold and the money buys a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished animal cannot go on the מזבח. Its holiness moves into the money it is sold for. That money must then be used for a proper חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets aside (designates) an animal or money for a קרבן
An animal with a blemish, which makes it unfit for the מזבח
Its money, meaning the money received when it is sold

phrases.english: One who designates a sin offering,
and it is blemished —
he sells it, and brings another with its money.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת, וַהֲרֵי הִיא בַּעֲלַת מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of חטאת cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blemished חטאת is sold, and its money buys a new חטאת.

steps.title: If the replacement was already brought, the first animal dies
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון rules that if the new חטאת was brought before the blemished one was slaughtered, the blemished one must die, because the owner already got כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: if the second animal was offered before the first one was slaughtered, the first one must die, because the owner already received atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון adds a twist. If the new animal was offered while the old blemished animal is still alive, the old one is left to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old animal was sold and is no longer holy. Even so, once the owner got כפרה from the new one while the old one was still alive, the old one is treated as a חטאת whose owners already got atonement. Such a חטאת must die.

keyTerms.meaning: Was offered on the מזבח
It must die, meaning it is locked away until it dies
The owners have already received atonement

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:
If the second one was offered
before it was slaughtered —
phrases.notes: "It" is the first, blemished animal, before the buyer slaughtered it for eating.

phrases.english: it must die, for the owners have already received atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a dissenting limit to the ruling in step 30
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the replacement חטאת was offered before the blemished one was slaughtered, the blemished one must die.

steps.title: Reading the רישא closely: who holds this view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from the משנה's first case that the old חטאת dies only because the replacement was already offered. If it was only set aside, the old one grazes. Then it asks whose view this is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason it dies is that he already offered another in its place. But if he did not offer another in its place, it grazes. Whose view is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts its discussion. It reads the משנה's first case closely and asks which תנא wrote it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא said the found חטאת dies when a replacement "was offered." So if the replacement was only set aside and not yet offered, the first one is not left to die. It just grazes until it gets a מום. The גמרא wants to know who holds this.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is... (used to read a rule closely and learn its opposite)
But, if not... (introduces the opposite case)
It grazes until it gets a מום, then it is sold
Whose view is this?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 30. Here "the רישא" means the משנה's earlier case of a lost חטאת that was later found, not the blemished animal.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The reason is that he offered another in its place,

phrases.aramaic: הָא לֹא הִקְרִיב אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ — רוֹעָה.
phrases.english: but if he did not offer another in its place, it grazes.
Whose view is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה text to a close reading of its first clause
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a found חטאת only grazes if the replacement was merely set aside?

steps.title: The רישא follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The רישא matches the רבנן, who hold that a חטאת lost at the time the replacement was set aside goes to graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the view of the רבנן, who say: an animal lost at the time of setting aside the replacement grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The רישא follows the רבנן from the earlier argument with רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, in step 29, the חכמים held that a חטאת only dies if it was found after the owner already got כפרה. That fits the close reading: if the replacement was only set aside, the old one grazes.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view
Lost at the time the replacement was set aside

phrases.english: It is the Rabbis, who say:
one that was lost at the time of setting aside the replacement grazes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מַנִּי question

steps.title: Reading the סיפא closely: the lost money case
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says that with lost money that was replaced, he buys a חטאת from both sums and the rest goes to נדבה. Read closely, this means that if he used only one sum, the other goes to ים המלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now say the last part: one who sets aside money for a חטאת, it is lost, and he sets aside other money in its place, brings from both, and the rest goes to free-will offerings. The reason is that he used both. But if he used only one of them, he must throw the other into the Dead Sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a problem. It reads the סיפא of the same משנה closely, and that reading points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using both sums only works if the first money was found before he bought the חטאת. The close reading shows that if he used only one sum, the other goes to ים המלח, even though it was found before he got כפרה. That is a strict view, not the רבנן's, since they say money goes to ים המלח only if found after כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the last part (look at the end of the same source)
Money
Free-will offerings (here, communal ones)
The Dead Sea, where holy money is thrown so nobody can use it

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
One who designates money for a sin offering, and it was lost,
and he designated other money in its place —
he should bring from this and from that,
phrases.notes: The first money was found before he bought the animal, so both sums are in his hands.

phrases.english: and the rest goes to free-will offerings.
The reason is that he brought from this and from that,
but if he brought from one of them —
he must take the second to the Dead Sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the סיפא against the attribution of the רישא
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that this משנה follows the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A close reading of the סיפא gives a stricter rule than the רבנן allow.

steps.title: The סיפא follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: The close reading of the סיפא matches רבי, who holds that a חטאת lost at the time the replacement was set aside must die.
steps.simpleTranslation: We arrive at רבי, who said: one that was lost at the time of setting aside the replacement must die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the סיפא matches רבי's view, the opposite of the רישא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, being lost when the replacement was set aside is enough to send the extra one to die, or for money, to ים המלח. That fits the strict close reading of the סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: We have arrived at (the view of)...
Must die

phrases.english: We have arrived at Rabbi, who said:
one that was lost at the time of setting aside the replacement dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the author that the close reading of the סיפא points to

steps.title: Can one משנה follow two different views?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רישא could follow the רבנן while the סיפא follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first part follows the רבנן and the last part follows רבי?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the problem clearly. It is strange for one משנה to switch authors in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a משנה is read as one consistent view. Steps 33 and 35 split it between two opposing תנאים, and the גמרא does not accept that easily.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: The first clause is the Rabbis, and the latter clause is Rabbi?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the two attributions into a challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: Splitting the משנה between the רבנן and רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One משנה should not hold two opposite views at once.

steps.title: It works out according to רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer: the problem is solved according to רב הונא, who quotes רב. His statement comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works out well according to רב הונא, as רב הונא said in the name of רב:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to bring רב הונא's statement in the name of רב, which will fix the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "הניחא" means a certain view has no problem here. This hints that for another view the question will still stand. The actual words of רב come right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one view, hinting at a problem for another)

phrases.english: This works out well according to Rav Huna,
as Rav Huna said that Rav said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the challenge in step 36
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an אמורא's view that removes the contradiction (continues next)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems split between the רבנן and רבי
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רב הונא, the משנה can be explained without a contradiction
